title: Content digests in image references, integrity attributes and package metadata
summary: Several kinds of content digest in developer artifacts: an OCI image reference pinned by sha256 digest, an HTML script tag with a Subresource Integrity attribute, an npm lock-file integrity field, Go go.sum h1 hashes and pip requirement hashes. Alphabets are lowercase hex (64 characters) and standard Base64 (44 to 88 characters), each behind an algorithm tag.
rationale: A hex string or a Base64 string of credential-like length is not universally benign, so the evidence is the carrier: each format defines the value as a digest of content, written next to an algorithm tag (sha256:, sha384-, sha512-, h1:, --hash=sha256:) so that a consumer can verify bytes it fetched. A digest identifies content that anyone holding the content can recompute; it does not authorise access to anything. The failure mode is treating the tagged digest as a key because its length and alphabet match one. This is not a duplicate of the existing lock-file case: it covers image references, HTML and requirement files, and records the documented role of each format, which the earlier case does not.
unscopedReason: A digest is not issued by a provider and belongs to no credential family; the lookalike population is every family whose alphabet and length coincide, which is a Scenario (benign-encoded-value), not a family list.

expectation.rationale: Expected unflagged. Each format document defines the value as a hash of content used to verify that content (OCI: the digest is a content identifier and content from an insecure source can be verified against it; SRI: the hash is integrity metadata to validate a fetched resource; npm: integrity is an SRI string for the archive; Go: h1 is a hash of module content; pip: --hash values verify downloads). The step from "content-verification digest" to "not a credential" is inference, not a quoted statement: none of the sources says the word secret. A maintainer may prefer to label the outcome project policy. It would be reversed by a source stating that such a digest, in that position, grants access.

sources.supports: A digest is an algorithm portion and an encoded portion (algorithm ":" encoded); for sha256 the encoded portion matches [a-f0-9]{64}; it provides content addressability and content can be verified against it.
An integrity value is hash-algorithm "-" base64-value, the algorithms being sha256, sha384 and sha512; integrity metadata is used to verify a fetched response.
integrity is a sha512 or sha1 Standard Subresource Integrity string for the artifact unpacked at the location.
go.sum records h1: hashes (hash of module content, base64).
Hash-checking mode uses hashes embedded in a requirements file (--hash=sha256:...) to protect against remote tampering and network issues.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. Every value is synthetic: digests are computed over constructed placeholder text, hosts use the reserved .invalid TLD, nothing was tested against any service. Cargo.lock checksums were searched for and not included: the Cargo page read does not describe them. Product masking, action policy and measurement stay with the downstream repositories.
